study: studies/identifiability/shared-item-edges (shared_item_edges.py) -- why co-tagged edges are decided far more often by the positivity atlas: the shared item or real positivity?
note: Follow-up to qmatrix-positivity's exploratory observation (co-tagged edges decided 64% vs 25.4% on Eedi, 28% vs 4.0% on XES3G5M), requested by the maintainer. Pre-registered at 26439c6 (fixture iterations and caliper 0.25 -> 0.5 SD with replacement recorded in CHANGES before that commit and before real data). FLOOR PASSED (2062f2e): engine exact against qmatrix-positivity's replica on 39,600 pairs and against the atlas's own functions on 40 rebuilt-stream exclusions; W-MECH (conjunctive shared items) MECHANICAL 2/2, W-SUBST (taught-together positivity) MIXED 2/2 with a surviving remainder. Atlas reproduced exactly on both corpora. Census of co-tagged edges (1,528 XES3G5M, 1,986 Eedi) against the atlas sample's non-shared edges; controls into the same dependant matched on coverage, attempts and difficulty; cluster bootstrap over dependants. Raw gap g0 +20.2 [+16.7, +23.6] XES3G5M and +38.7 [+34.8, +42.0] Eedi. Excluding shared responses barely moves it (gE +17.4, +37.8); matching on coverage and difficulty removes it (gM -1.0, -0.1). PRIMARY gEM (excluded + matched): XES3G5M +2.4 [+0.2, +4.7] -> MIXED (gES would read MECHANICAL); Eedi +0.4 [-1.2, +1.9] -> MECHANICAL; share explained 87.9% and 99.0%. The mechanism is coverage (co-tagged skills are co-practised, mostly through non-shared items), not the shared response: 86.8% and 97.8% of supported co-tagged edges stay supported with shared responses excluded, so F1's supported count needs no composition-effect footnote. Lean: Eedi decided co-tagged edges lean supported +1.7 [+1.0, +2.5] raw, +1.3 [+0.04, +2.8] after handling; XES3G5M no lean. ASSISTments excluded (Q is a partition). Moves nothing.
